verses.text: After this I saw another angel coming down from heaven. He had great authority, and the earth was lit up by his glory.
He called out in a mighty voice: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the Great! She has become a home for demons, a prison for every impure spirit, and a cage for every unclean and hated bird.
For all the nations have drunk the maddening wine of her immorality. The kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth grew rich from her excessive luxury.”
Then I heard another voice from heaven say: “Come out of her, my people, so you won’t share in her sins or receive any of her plagues.
Her sins are piled up to heaven, and God has remembered her crimes.
Give her back what she gave; pay her back double for what she did. Mix her a double portion in her own cup.
Give her as much torment and grief as the glory and luxury she gave herself. In her heart she says, ‘I sit as a queen. I’m not a widow, and I’ll never mourn.’
So in one day her plagues will come: death, grief, and famine. She’ll be consumed by fire, because the Lord God who judges her is powerful.”
When the kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality and lived in luxury with her see the smoke of her burning, they’ll weep and mourn for her.
Terrified by her torment, they’ll stand far away and cry: “Woe! Woe to you, great city, mighty Babylon! In one hour your judgment has come!”
The merchants of the earth will weep and mourn for her, because no one buys their cargo anymore—
cargo of gold, silver, precious stones, pearls, fine linen, purple cloth, silk, scarlet cloth, all kinds of scented wood, ivory articles, expensive wood, bronze, iron, and marble;
cinnamon, spice, incense, perfume, frankincense, wine, olive oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, and human lives.
“They’ve lost the fruit they craved. All their luxury and splendor are gone, never to be found again.”
The merchants who sold these goods and grew rich from her will stand far away, terrified by her torment. They’ll weep and mourn,
saying, “Woe! Woe to the great city, dressed in fine linen, purple, and scarlet, glittering with gold, precious stones, and pearls!
In one hour all this wealth has been destroyed!” Every ship captain, passenger, sailor, and anyone who makes a living from the sea will stand far away.
When they see the smoke of her burning, they’ll cry out, “Was there ever a city like this great city?”
They’ll throw dust on their heads and cry, weeping and mourning: “Woe! Woe to the great city, where everyone who had ships on the sea became rich from her wealth! In one hour she’s been ruined!”
Rejoice over her, heaven! Rejoice, God’s people, apostles and prophets! For God has judged her for the way she treated you.
Then a mighty angel picked up a stone like a huge millstone and threw it into the sea, saying: “With such violence Babylon the great city will be thrown down, never to be found again.

The music of harpists, musicians, flute players, and trumpeters will never be heard in you again. No worker of any trade will ever be found in you again. The sound of a millstone will never be heard in you again.

The light of a lamp will never shine in you again. The voices of a bridegroom and bride will never be heard in you again. Your merchants were the earth’s powerful people, and all nations were deceived by your sorcery.
In her was found the blood of prophets and God’s holy people, and of all who have been killed on earth.”
